brief_title: Efficacy And Safety of Olatorepatide in Adults With Overweight or Obesity Without Diabetes
official_title: A Phase 3, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Olatorepatide, a GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist, in Participants Living With Overweight or Obesity Without Diabetes (RISE-1)
brief_summary:
This study will test olatorepatide (study drug) to determine whether it can help treat overweight or obesity.

In this study we will test how safe and how well olatorepatide works compared to placebo in people who are overweight or obese but do not have diabetes.

The study is looking at:

* How well the study drug works
* How the body and blood and urine biomarkers change after taking the study drug, which can help researchers understand why the study drug may work better in some people than in others
* What side effects the study drug might cause
* How much of the study drug is in the blood at different times
* If the body makes antibodies to the study drug this may cause the study drug to not work as well

eligibility.criteria:
Key Inclusion Criteria:

1. Has BMI ≥30.0 kg/m\^2 at screening OR BMI ≥27.0 kg/m\^2 at screening with at least 1 of the following weight-related comorbidities: Hypertension, Dyslipidemia, Prediabetes, established Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA), established Coronary Artery Disease (CAD), Heart failure, established cerebrovascular disease, as described in the protocol
2. History of one or more self-reported unsuccessful dietary attempts to lose weight

Key Exclusion Criteria:

1. Have previous or current diagnosis of diabetes, including Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) or Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) or screening HbA1c ≥6.5% as described in the protocol
2. Change in body weight \>5 kg within 90 days prior to randomization as described in the protocol
3. Current use or previous treatment in 90 days prior to screening with GLP-1-RA, GLP-1/GIP RA, related molecule, or any other Nutrient-Stimulated Hormone (NuSH)-based therapy
4. Current treatment or treatment in 90 days prior to screening associated with weight loss or weight gain or high risk of initiation of such a treatment during the study duration as described in the protocol
5. Previous or planned bariatric surgery

Note: Other Protocol Defined Inclusion/ Exclusion Criteria Apply
